prompt: A map uses scale $1$ cm $: 50$ km. Two cities are $7$ cm apart on the map. What is the real distance?
hint: The scale works like a rate: each centimeter on the map always stands for the same real distance.

hints.text: The scale works like a rate: each centimeter on the map always stands for the same real distance.
One centimeter is $50$ km and the cities are $7$ centimeters apart, so multiply $7 \times 50$.
$7 \times 50 = 350$, so the cities are really $350$ km apart.

explanation: The scale $1$ cm $: 50$ km means every map centimeter represents $50$ real kilometers.
The map distance is $7$ of those centimeters, so multiply $7$ by $50$.
Use the fact $7 \times 5 = 35$ to see that the product $7 \times 50$ is $350$.
The real distance between the cities is $350$ km.
